rationale: A is more useful because it gives a clearer recommendation tailored to the stated goal and includes a meaningful caveat: platform-native share formats are high-variance, so F+C is framed as a more robust expected-value choice. That uncertainty handling is decision-relevant. B also gives a concrete recommendation, but its support is more generic, with KPI definitions and thresholds that don’t clearly discriminate among the feature options, and it lacks explicit caveats. Neither provides strong quantitative backing or a clearly stated main alternative/revisit trigger, but A better connects the recommendation to downside risk and first-month reach.
